proposed.text: A decorative pattern features bold, angular, deeply carved geometric forms on wooden frames, door panels, and roof support brackets. It combines Islamic geometric principles with indigenous Southeast Asian aesthetics. Name this decorative tradition.

options.text: Arabesque — interlocking Middle Eastern vegetal/geometric pattern
Okir — the Maranao geometric relief carving on wood frames and panels
Zellige — North African/Moroccan geometric tile work

proposed.rationale: The article defines okir as 'Geometric relief carving pattern characteristic of Maranao decorative tradition; appears on door frames, roof brackets, wall panels; combines Islamic geometry with indigenous aesthetic.' [A]: Arabesque is interlocking vegetal/geometric patterns from Middle Eastern Islamic tradition. [B]: Muqarnas is three-dimensional corbelled vaulting, not relief carving. [D]: Zellige is geometric tile work from North Africa/Morocco.
